author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty

given a specialty held by veterinarians, when the specialty directory is opened, then each holder is listed under it by first name, then last name, as in "Helen Leary"
given a veterinarian holding several specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is listed under each of them
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian does not appear on it
edge case 3: a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it
edge case 4: every specialty shows on one page, however many specialties and veterinarians the clinic has (no pagination)
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2 unchanged, per the owner's decision)
A navigation entry or any link from another page to the specialty directory (owner deferred it to a possible follow-up request)
Any search or filter input on the specialty directory (NG-9 stands; the directory is a listing, not a search)
A defined ordering of specialties or of veterinarians within a specialty (open question in docs/prd.md)
notes: Grounded in intake-decision line 1; both quoted decisions honored, Non-Goals table unchanged so no scope_overrides. Existing requirements bind the new page: REQ-SYS-001 (it carries the standard navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory; only a navigation entry leading TO it is excluded) and REQ-LANG-002 (every new wording key present in every supported language bundle; specialty names are data shown as recorded, not translated). author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory lives in the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure) and is built only from patterns already in force (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog). (1) A new read-only SpecialtyRepository returns every specialty, since edge case 3 needs unheld specialties. PetTypeRepository shows the precedent: one repository for a persisted lookup value. It extends Spring Data's minimal Repository, as VetRepository does, not JpaRepository (Design Principle 5, minimal surface). (2) A new SpecialtyDirectory value object (the UL term 'Specialty directory') holds the inversion rule as an immutable record: every specialty by recorded name, each with its holders' names first then last. It is built by a static factory from the specialties and the vets, uses defensive copies, and does no I/O (architecture-principles § Domain Core, closed properties). A vet holding nothing drops out naturally; an unheld specialty stays with an empty holder list. (3) A new SpecialtyController serves GET /specialties.html. It calls SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository.findAll() (cached), hands both to the factory, and puts the directory in the model; it holds no business rule (the Web controller row). (4) A new template under templates/vets/ reuses the fragments/layout call. system-design.md changes: three new Contracts rows (SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyController); REQ-VET-003 added to the Vet, Specialty and VetRepository rows; an invariant saying Specialty maps no association back to its holders; the vet/ package line; a new § Scale and Load section with the directory's row; and a corrected Threat Model mass-assignment row. Resolution basis: grep and read of vet/*.java, owner/PetTypeRepository.java, model/BaseEntity.java and the three controllers with @InitBinder. The IntelliJ oracle was not connected, so this is the weaker basis.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html binds no request input: no @RequestParam, no @ModelAttribute, no path variable. The binding target is therefore none. It still declares an @InitBinder that disallows "id" and "*.id", as the owner, pet and visit controllers do (security-principles § Realization, mass-assignment row: 'a new controller or binder that omits the disallow list fails').

Double at the domain boundary: none. SpecialtyDirectoryTests build real Vet and Specialty objects through their setters, as VetControllerTests does. These unit tests carry the rules: holder naming, a vet listed under each specialty they hold, a no-specialty vet omitted, an unheld specialty listed with no holders, and every specialty present (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: real implementations first).

Double at the repository boundary in SpecialtyControllerTests: hand-written fakes of VetRepository (two findAll methods) and SpecialtyRepository (one method), registered as beans in the @WebMvcTest slice through a nested @TestConfiguration. The @MockitoBean stubbing in VetControllerTests is tolerated legacy and is not to be copied (testing-principles § Mocking Policy, 'Mock-framework stubs are tolerated, not encouraged').

Double at the framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy). It asserts the view name, the model attribute, and rendered names in the HTML, and that the page has no pagination control.

Real repository check: one test in ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest on the H2 seed) proves SpecialtyRepository returns all three seeded specialties. No double is needed, following that class's existing vet-finding test.

Template: the layout fragment's menu argument must match no nav item (for example 'specialties'), so no existing nav entry is shown active. No nav entry or link to /specialties.html is added (PRD non-goal; the REQ-SYS-001 layout still carries the standard navigation). Specialty and vet names render with th:text only, never th:utext (security-principles § Realization, XSS row).

Wording: reuse the existing message keys where they fit (specialties, vets, name). Any new key goes into all eleven bundles under src/main/resources/messages/. I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces this and also rejects literal text in the template (REQ-LANG-002). Specialty names are data and are not translated.

The controller calls VetRepository.findAll(), the no-argument cached method. Today only the machine-readable /vets route calls it, and that route is a Known Defect pending removal (system-design § Known Defects). Once this controller lands, removing that route must keep the method.

patterns.description: repository for a persisted lookup value; SpecialtyRepository follows it, but extends the minimal Repository like VetRepository
constructor-injected repository, GET handler returning a vets/ view name; the new controller mirrors it without pagination
@InitBinder disallowing id and *.id, the shape the new controller copies
layout fragment call, table markup, #{} message keys, and th:text rendering of names

risks.risk: BaseEntity defines no equals or hashCode, so a Specialty compares by identity. The cached vet graph and the specialties read per request are separate instances of the same rows. Grouping keyed on Specialty instances puts every holder under nothing.
risks.mitigation: Group by specialty identifier (getId), not by the Specialty instance. The unit test builds the specialty list and the vets' specialties as separate instances sharing an id, so this failure is caught (system-design § Contracts invariant: 'matching specialties by identifier').

risks.risk: Path scales with data: the directory reads every specialty and every veterinarian on one unpaged page (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty directory row; PRD edge case 4).
risks.mitigation: Use the simplest readable form, a bounded path: one pass building a map from specialty id to holders, then one pass over the specialties. No pagination and no query-level join.

risks.risk: Specialty ordering: the PRD commits to no order (non-goal, open question), and a hash-map build could render in a varying order.
risks.mitigation: Keep the iteration order of the specialty list the repository returns (a LinkedHashMap or a list walk). Tests assert membership, not order, so the open question stays open.

risks.risk: New public endpoint widens the exposed surface (security-principles § Realization, 'Widening the exposed surface' row).
risks.mitigation: GET only and read-only. It shows specialty names and veterinarian names, both already public through /vets.html. It mutates nothing and exposes no identifier.

notes: Autofix audit: the log has no design-doc-autofix records, so there was nothing to audit. ADR: none written. The in-memory inversion replaces a bidirectional Specialty-to-Vet mapping. That alternative would add an eager association and a serialization cycle on the /vets route, and it is ruled out within this slice only: nothing it decides constrains a later slice (adr-template § When to Create an ADR). The design doc carries it as a state line. Threat Model correction: the mass-assignment row said every controller disallows id binding. VetController, WelcomeController and CrashController declare no binder (they bind no form), so the row now names the controllers that do. The § Scale and Load section was absent from system-design.md; it is added from the harness doctor template with this slice's row only (demand-driven). Brief observation for the security brief's owner, not a blocker: the mass-assignment row's literal rule ('a new controller ... that omits the disallow list fails') applies even to a controller that binds nothing. This design follows it as written.

author: change-grader
summary: add read-only specialty directory page at /specialties.html

blast_radius.note: Additive and contained to the vet package: three new production files, one new template, two new test classes, one appended repository test, and the three briefs. No existing production line changes, nothing under a sensitive path, and the one security-surface path is a new read-only GET that binds no request input and shows names /vets.html already makes public.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do what the description says. SpecialtyDirectory.of groups holders by Integer id through a HashMap (value equality, not instance identity), lists every specialty from its own repository so an unheld one still appears, and skips vets with no specialty by construction. The template escapes output with th:text, and the layout menu argument 'specialties' matches no nav item, so no entry point appears. The one quiet property is ordering: specialties follow the repository's unordered findAll and holders follow the cached vet list, so display order depends on the database. The PRD records this as an open question rather than a commitment.

test_adequacy.note: The tests exercise real outcomes and would fail against plausible broken versions. Fresh Specialty instances per call catch a regression to instance matching. Exact listing equality catches a holder filed under the wrong specialty or a wrong name format. The omit and unheld-specialty cases each have a test. The MockMvc test renders 31 specialties and asserts no page= link, and the seeded-DB test proves findAll returns all three rows. Ordering is not asserted, which matches the PRD's decision not to commit to an order.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four round-1 reviewers approved with cited evidence, and the citations I checked resolve (SpecialtyController.java:44 and :49, SpecialtyRepository.java:36, messages.properties:21-23). Reading the PRD settles it: edge case 1 covers a veterinarian's own specialty list, and the new open question records that REQ-VET-003 commits to no order. The other recommendations are polish.

scope_deviation.note: The diff delivers exactly the intake's bullets: GET /specialties.html, recorded names, first-then-last holder names, vets with no specialty omitted, one unpaged page, read-only, and no navigation link. It had zero retries, consultations, or design revisions. The doc edits beyond the new entry are a new Scale and Load row for the page and a threat-model row that now correctly lists which controllers declare the id disallow list. Both describe this slice's surface.

rationale: A contained, additive read-only page whose inversion logic, tests, and docs match the intake. The approvals are well cited, and the only residual question, display order, is recorded in the PRD as an open question. A glance at SpecialtyDirectory.of and the template confirms it.
